correctness.rationale: For each finite natural spline, endpoint-reflection of its secants yields a periodic whole-line forcing whose unique bounded tridiagonal Green solution is odd at both boundary knots. The computed infinite convolution derivative operator has explicit coefficient L1 norm bounded by sqrt(3) on every cell. Constant reproduction plus centered secants proves the contrast sufficiency. On 2m cells alternating positive secants yield exact boundary derivative (a_m-R a_{m-1})/(a_m-a_{m-1}); quotient recurrence decreases to 2+sqrt(3), proving sharpness on finite grids. Signed alternation proves sharpness of the operator bound. The packaged symbolic identities and independent finite linear solves passed; numerical sampling is not treated as a proof.

value.rationale: The sharp all-grid contrast ratio provides a directly usable quantitative decision rule for when an ordinary smooth natural interpolant can replace a nonlinear monotone scheme without introducing nonphysical turns. The exact derivative operator norm is a structural stability invariant and the long-grid alternating obstruction establishes necessity for the uniform guarantee. A previously treated four-knot ratio of 4 is insufficient for arbitrary grid length; the new constant 2+sqrt(3) is not a cosmetic reparameterization.
